title: Magic Is Normal or a Big Deal?
use_cases: Use when distinguishing between high fantasy and magical realism genres
Implement when defining how characters should react to supernatural events in a narrative
Configure when establishing the tone and atmosphere of a fictional setting
content:
This is the second big clue. Ask: How do people in the story react to the magic?

In fantasy, magic is a big deal. When a dragon breathes fire, people run. When a wizard casts a spell, it is a moment of power. The magic is the point of the story. It is the supernatural force that changes things.

In magical realism, magic is not a big deal at all. It is presented in a deadpan, normal way. In One Hundred Years of Solitude, a character ascends to heaven while folding laundry. The other characters are a bit sad she is gone, but they are not shocked that a person just floated away. The magic is treated as mundane. This is a key part of the narrative style differences between the two.
